subject: Were they only told to take off the badge?
alt: Cartoon: big feet in khaki shorts, green socks and black shoes, with a lathi (stick) at the side. Two ordinary men standing nearby ask each other: Were they only told to take off the badge?
chutki: There is no face in this cartoon, only khaki shorts, socks, shoes and a lathi. Dhodapkar knows that some identities are complete with the uniform alone. The two ordinary people standing in front are as small as their stature has been kept in this picture.

'Were they only told to take off the badge?' The whole satire is in this one question: the badge has come off, everything else is just as it was. There is a big difference between hiding an identity and changing a way of thinking, and this cartoon puts its finger on that difference.
